domain: Marine time service and chronometer rating — the observatory time signal, the rating certificate, the going rate, the hack watch carried below, logged discontinuities, and the rule against rating a clock against another clock of its own rank.
axioms: No clock is right. A usable value is a reading, plus a rate, plus the interval elapsed since the last comparison against a higher authority; a bare reading with no interval attached is not evidence.

Authority is a chain terminating in an observatory signal. Two instruments of the same rank agreeing establishes agreement, never truth, so a test that sets both sides of a comparison proves nothing about either.
A carried correction is valid only across the interval its rate was measured over; preferring an older carried value to a live signal requires an explicit bound on its age.

An unlogged discontinuity — a stoppage, a reset, an instrument carried ashore and returned — voids every correction derived before it, and the classic loss comes from a step nobody recorded rather than from a rate nobody measured.
Most error enters at the unrated intermediary: the hack watch between the chronometer room and the point of use is the link no certificate covers.

An error that is steady can be applied as a correction; an error that merely looks steady because only its sign or its name is being recorded is the dangerous case, and only its magnitude distinguishes them.

An instrument with no failure indication is indistinguishable from a working one, and an alarm that fires on schedule stops being read; the rating certificate exists because neither silence nor routine noise survives as information.
primitives: sign versus magnitude of an error
failure_mode: Models the world as a single scalar carried by a small number of ranked instruments, so it systematically misses set-shaped questions: which files exist, which directories were walked, what was never placed under comparison at all.
Treats content as undifferentiated — it can ask how stale a copy is but not what the copy contains, so a textual rule's evadability and a comparison surface's completeness fall outside it.
Inclined to accept any proxy that carries a rating, so it can under-detect a proxy that is well-behaved and measuring the wrong mechanism entirely unless explicitly pointed at the consumer.

Assumes a single authoritative reference exists and is identifiable; where the reference is itself plural or contested it will pick one and reason confidently from it rather than questioning the choice.
Its instinct on every uncertainty is to add a comparison, so it will propose more frequent or more instrumented checking where the cheaper fix is to remove the derived value altogether.
